newsitem.title: USA: US stocks end edgy session mixed, retailers firm.
newsitem.headline: US stocks end edgy session mixed, retailers firm.

text.p: Wall Street stocks turned in a mixed performance on Thursday, as retailers rallied on strong sales figures but tech stocks succumbed to more profit-taking.
The Dow industrials rose 26 points to close unofficially at 6773, led by Sears, Roebuck and Co, which rose 1-3/8 to 49-7/8 after reporting strong sales growth in January.

"Several companies gave us better-than-expected numbers, and we got some good activity in the group for the first time in a long time," said Philip Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management.
Retail analysts said apparel companies were standouts, with chain stores such as Gap Inc and Limited Inc as well as key department stores posting strong numbers.
Gap shares rose 2-3/8 to 32-1/4, Limited gained 1/4 to 17-3/8, and Wal-Mart Stores Inc rose 1/2 to 23-5/8.

Still, the buying interest was clearly tempered, as investors warily awaited key employment and wage data due on Friday. Financial markets often become volatile after surprises in the report, considered a key leading indicator of inflation.
"I don't think anyone was going to take an extreme position going into tomorrow's numbers," Orlando said.

Economists surveyed by Reuters expect the report to show the nation's unemployment rate dipped in January to 5.2 percent from 5.3 percent, while average hourly wages are expected to show a modest 0.2 percent increase.
Technology stocks remained under pressure, as investors backed away from the top-tier names that led the most recent leg of the stock market's rally.
Intel Corp fell 4-1/8 to 153-1/8, bringing losses on the high-flying shares to 11-5/8 points over the last two sessions. Microsoft Corp fell 1-1/4 to 97-1/8.
"We saw a restless rotation in the market today, and tech stocks lacked the sponsorship and the bounce they once had," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co.

Still, the intense selling pressure of the previous session clearly eased, and analysts said several issues appeared to find support after their recent losses. Cisco Systems Inc rose 7/8 to 63-7/8, and Gateway 2000 Inc added 1-3/4 to 57-1/4.
Almost forgotten by the end of the session was the much-awaited morning release of President Bill Clinton's fiscal 1998 budget.
The budget blueprint was considered a test of credibility on the path to a balanced federal budget by 2002.
Stocks showed little response to the presentation, even though many Wall Street professionals scoffed at the budget's assumptions.

"There's a lot of -- I don't even want to call it smoke and mirrors -- it's just plain garbage that is embedded in how they got to a surplus budget in 2002," said Michael Strauss, senior vice president and chief economist at Sanwa Securities in New York.
Shares in oil companies were lower after a sharp retreat in crude prices. Texaco Inc fell 1-1/2 to 103-7/8, Chevron Corp fell 1/4 to 65-3/8 and Mobil Corp dipped 3/4 to 129-1/2.
In individual issues, USA Detergents Inc slid 13-7/8 to 20-3/8 after the company warned of weaker-than-expected fourth-quarter earnings.
Manpower Inc surged 5-3/8 to 35-3/8, after the company reported higher fourth-quarter earnings and said its European operations showed signs of recovering.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.04 to 1346.40.
The S&P 500 index rose 1.87 to 780.15.
The Russell 2000 index of small cap stocks fell 0.01 to 365.48.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
